has the single empty neighbour D4.  D4 is a legal capture now:
4…B D4 removes the whole R–B5–D5 complex.  Hence 1.W D3 does not survive
best defence, and in particular it does not give White a forced net on the
left.

With the defence 1.W D3 in place the left side is

C1–C2 : {B1,B2}
A2    : {A1,A3,B2}
B3–B4 : {A3,A4,B2}

The only moves that touch a black liberty are A1,A3,A4,B1,B2.  After the
mandatory 1.W D3

* 2.W B1 forces 2…B B2. B B2 connects A2 B3 B4 C1 C2 into one group G with
A1 A3 A4 and the White B1 stone is in atari on A1. 3…B A1 captures the
sacrificial stone and G retains A3 A4. 4.W A3 is met by 5.B A4 and 4.W A4
is met by 5.B A3, the classic A3/A4 snap-back.

* 2.W B2 is in atari on B1. Black is forced to 2…B B1 which captures the
sacrificial W B2 and makes B1–C1–C2 with {A1,B2}.  A2 is now {A1,A3} and
B3–B4 is {A3,A4}.  A1 and B2 are suicide for White and 3.W A3 is met by
4.B A4 capturing the net stone, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 and 5.B A5.
Black can always keep the false liberties A1/B2 and recapture the White
A3/A4 net stone.

A1,A3,A4 are self-atari or are captured at once.  No first White move,
and in particular no move after the compulsory 1.W D3 defence, forces a
capture of a Black group against best Black defence.  The forced-kill set
is therefore empty.

public_text.5:
{B2}
B2 is the only first move that simultaneously reduces the three black chains on the left. C1-C2 lives on B1 and B2, A2 lives on A1 A3 B2 and B3-B4 lives on A3 A4 B2. Taking B2 removes the common breathing point and the connection.

1.W B2 puts C1-C2 in atari on B1 and the white B2 stone itself is in atari on B1. Black cannot ignore C1-C2.

If 2.B B1, the sacrificial W B2 is captured and B1-C1-C2 is formed with the outside liberties A1 and B2. A2 is now A1 A3 B2 and B3-B4 is A3 A4 B2. A1 and B2 are suicide for White, so the only useful reductions are A3 and A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 which captures the net stone and restores two liberties to the B1-C1-C2-A2-B3-B4 complex; 3.W A4 is met symmetrically. In both lines after the forced B1 capture White obtains the shared liberty grab on A1 A3 A4 and the left side runs out of liberties first.

If Black tries 2.B A3 or 2.B A4 instead of B1, White plays 3.W B1 and C1-C2 dies at once because its only remaining liberty after W B2 is B1. The A2 stone then loses B2 and is left with only A1.

By contrast 1.W B1 is not a forced kill. After 1.W B1 Black can play 2.B B2 in perfect safety. B2 connects A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 into one six-stone group G with the three outside liberties A1 A3 A4 and the white B1 stone is now in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1 and G is left with A3 A4 B1. The supposed self-atari of B2 disappears once the connection is made and the A1/A3/A4 race is won by Black. B1 is therefore a sacrifice, not a forced capture of the left side, whereas B2 initiates the genuine forced reduction of the whole corner.
public_text.1:
{B2}
B2 is the only first move that touches the three weak black chains on the left at once and forces a capture. C1-C2 lives on B1 and B2, A2 lives on A1 A3 B2 and B3-B4 lives on A3 A4 B2. Taking B2 therefore removes the common connecting and breathing point and puts C1-C2 in atari on B1 while cutting A2 away from B3-B4.

1. W B2 puts C1-C2 down to the single liberty B1 and the sacrificial white stone itself is in atari on B1. Black cannot ignore C1-C2. 2. B B1 is the only useful defence; it captures the white B2 stone and makes B1-C1-C2 with the outside liberties A1 and B2. After that A2 is left on A1 A3, B3-B4 is left on A3 A4, and the white wall on the right already controls A4.

From here White has the forced net on A1/A3/A4. If Black tries 2. B A3 or 2. B A4 instead of B1, White plays 3. W B1 and C1-C2 is captured at once because its only remaining liberty after W B2 is B1. In every line Black spends a move on B1 to save C1-C2 and in doing so gives White the shared liberty grab that finishes the left side.

By contrast 1. W B1 is not forcing. After 1. W B1 C1-C2 is in atari on B2 but the white stone on B1 is itself in immediate atari on A1. 2. B B2 is legal and connects A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 into a six-stone group G with the three outside liberties A1 A3 A4, while W B1 is now in atari on A1 and can be taken with 3. B A1. The supposed self-atari of B2 disappears once the connection is made and the B1 sacrifice is immediately threatened. This is the refutation Colleague1, Colleague14 and Colleague5 already gave and it is why an unsupported {B1} from Colleague12 does not hold up.

The {} lines rely on snap-backs on A3/A4 after 2. B B1, but after 1. W B2 2. B B1 the B1-C1-C2 group is already isolated with A1 as its last real outside liberty, and A2 and B3-B4 have lost B2. White gets the capture before Black can restore two separate liberties. B2 is therefore the unique first move that initiates a genuine forced reduction of the whole left side.
public_text.9:
{}
The corner has to be defended before any left-side attack can be tried.

The White group D1-D2 is in atari on the board as drawn. The only liberties that keep it alive are E1, E2 and D3, and D3 is the only one that actually increases the group’s liberty count. Any first move that is not 1.W D3 allows 2...B D3 and the D1-D2 wall is removed, so the only admissible first move in a forced line is 1.W D3.

After 1.W D3 the left side is the only place where Black can be put in atari. The only points that touch the C1-C2 pair are B1 and B2.

1.W B1 → C1-C2 is in atari on B2. Black is forced to 2.B B2, which connects A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 into the six-stone group G. G now has the three outside liberties A1, A3, A4 and the White stone on B1 is itself in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1 and G is left with A3, A4, B1. A further 4.W A3 is met by 5.B A4 which recaptures the net stone, and 4.W A4 is met by 5.B A3. The A1/B1 race is a snap-back and Black can always keep at least two real liberties on the left.

1.W B2 → C1-C2 is in atari on B1 and the White B2 stone is itself in atari on B1. The only saving move is 2.B B1 which captures W B2 and forms B1-C1-C2 with the liberties A1, B2. A2 is on A1, A3, B2 and B3-B4 is on A3, A4, B2. A1 and B2 are suicide for White, so the only reductions are A3/A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone, and 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 followed by a recapture. Black can always restore a liberty on A1/A3/A4/B2 and the snap-back holds.

A1, A3, A4 are immediate self-atari or are captured at once by B B1, B A4 or B B2, and any other first move loses D1-D2 to 2...B D3. Hence even the two ostensibly threatening first moves B1 and B2 are met by forced captures of the White net stone and Black can keep the left corner alive. No first White move therefore forces a capture of a Black group against best defence, so the set of forcing killing first moves is empty.
public_text.13:
{B2}
B2 is the only first move that touches the three weak black chains on the left simultaneously. C1-C2 lives on B1 and B2, A2 lives on A1 A3 B2 and B3-B4 lives on A3 A4 B2. Taking B2 removes the common breathing point and puts C1-C2 into immediate atari on B1.

After 1.W B2 Black cannot ignore C1-C2. 2.B B1 is forced to save it and it captures the sacrificial W B2, making B1-C1-C2 with the outside liberties A1 and B2. After the capture B2 is white, so the real liberty count of B1-C1-C2 is A1 alone. A2 is now left on A1 A3 and B3-B4 is left on A3 A4, with the white wall B5-C3-C4 already controlling A4.

From here White has the net. 3.W A1 threatens B1-C1-C2 at once and also reduces A2. If Black tries 3...B A3, 4.W B1 is illegal because B1 is occupied, so 4.W A1 captures B1-C1-C2 on its last liberty while A2 is already cut off from B2. If Black tries 3...B A4 the same A1 capture is immediate and B3-B4 loses A4. The only Black try that keeps A1 is 3...B A1, but that loses B1-C1-C2 at once to 4.W B1? Actually 4.W B1 is taken, so C1-C2 dies and A2-B3-B4 is left on A3 A4.

The B1-first line is not forcing. 1.W B1 puts C1-C2 in atari on B2 but White B1 itself is on A1 and B2. 2.B B2 connects A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 into a six stone group G with the three outside liberties A1 A3 A4 and White B1 is now in atari on A1. Black then restores liberties and captures the sacrifice. The D1-D2 defence myth used to support {} is also false: D1-D2 has E1, D3 and E2 as liberties, so 1...B D3 is not a forced refutation of any non-D3 first move.

Hence the central squeeze at B2 is the unique move that creates a genuine forced reduction of the whole left side irrespective of Black’s reply, and no other first move does.
public_text.14:
{}
The only first moves that can put a black group into atari are B1 and B2, and both are answered by a forced capture of the White net stone and by the need to defend the right side.

If 1.W B1, C1–C2 is in atari on B2. Black does not have to let it die. 2.B B2 is legal and connects A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into one six-stone group G. After the connection G has the outside liberties A1, A3, A4 and the white stone on B1 is now itself in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1. The big black group is left on A3, A4, B1 and any White reduction on A3/A4 is a snap-back: 4.W A3 is met by 5.B A4 capturing the net stone, and the same holds for 4.W A4. The race for the shared liberty A1 is won by Black and the left side stays alive.

If 1.W B2, C1–C2 is in atari on B1 and the white stone on B2 is itself in atari on B1. Black is forced to 2.B B1, capturing the sacrificial W B2 and making B1–C1–C2 with liberties A1, B2. A2 is left on A1, A3, B2 and B3–B4 is left on A3, A4, B2. A1 and B2 are suicide for White and the only legal reductions are A3/A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 and the black groups keep the false liberties A1, B2. No net closes.

Any first move that is not B1/B2 touches no black liberty and is answered at once by Black. In particular the right side cannot be ignored: the D1–D2 group is the first thing that must be met. Any first move ≠ D3 is answered immediately by 2…B D3 and White is forced to defend the right before the left can be closed. After the forced defence 1.W D3 the White wall becomes D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with liberties D4, C5 and the left side is no longer a forced kill. A1, A3, A4 are self-atari or are captured at once by B B1, B A4, B A3.

Hence B1 and B2 are both met by a forced capture of the White net stone and a defence of the right side, and no other first move touches a black liberty. No first White move forces a capture of a black group against best defence, so the forced-kill set is empty.
public_text.4:
The White D1–D2 two stone group is on the edge of the board. 
After 1… the group has only the one real liberty D3, the points E1/E2 being
off the board.  Hence

* 1.W ≠ D3  2.B D3  and White loses D1–D2 at once.

So any serious line has to start with

1.W D3

The White wall D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 is then left with the two liberties D4 and
C5 and D4 and C5 are both suicide for Black after 1.W D3.  The Black corner
is

* Gc = B1–C1–C2 L={B1,B2}
* Ga = A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
* Gb = B3–B4 L={A3,A4,B2}

and after 1.W D3 Black can at once connect the corner.

* 1.W D3 2.B B2  merges Ga,Gb,Gc into
G = A2–B2–B3–B4–C1–C2 with L={A1,A3,A4,B1}.  
3.W B1 is met by 4.B A1 capturing B1, 3.W A1 is met by 4.B B1 capturing A1,
3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing A3, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 capturing A4.
The A1/B1 snap-back can always be kept alive and G never loses its second
liberty.

* 1.W D3 2.B B1  gives Gc = B1–C1–C2 L={A1,B2}, Ga L={A1,A3,B2},
Gb L={A3,A4,B2}. B2 is suicide for White and A1 is suicide for White.
3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3
etc.  Black can always recapture the White net stone first and keep at
least two liberties on A1/A3/A4/B2.

The same snap-back is obtained after 2.B A1, 2.B A3, 2.B A4.  No first move
B1/B2/A1/A3/A4 can be played without first losing the D1–D2 group to
2…B D3, and after the forced defence 1.W D3 Black can keep a second
liberty on the left side and capture every White sacrificial net stone
first.  Hence White has no first move which forces a capture of a Black
group against best defence.

{}
public_text.10:
{} 

The right-hand wall must be saved first.  D1–D2 is only alive on D3 so any
1.W ≠ D3 is answered by 2…B D3 and the D1–D2 two–stone group is removed at
once.  After the forced 1.W D3 the wall is D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two
liberties D4,C5 and

* C1–C2 : {B1,B2}
* A2    : {A1,A3,B2}
* B3–B4 : {A3,A4,B2}

Black to move can always keep a real liberty on the left corner.

2…B B1 makes B1–C1–C2 with {A1,B2}, A2 with {A1,A3,B2} and B3–B4 with
{A3,A4,B2}.  B2 and A1 are suicide for White and any White net A3/A4 is
immediately recaptured on A4/A3.

2…B B2 makes the six–stone group A2–B2–B3–B4–C1–C2 with {A1,A3,A4,B1}.
A White sacrifice on B1 is answered by 3…B A1 capturing the sacrifice
and restoring {A3,A4,B1} to the group; a White net on A3 is met by
…B A4 capturing the net stone and a White net on A4 is met by …B A3.
The same snap–back occurs after 2…B A1,2…B A3 or 2…B A4.  In particular
the B1 and B2 sacrifices are snap-backs and the liberty A1 can always
be kept.

Hence with best Black defence the left side stays alive and no first
White move, and in particular no move other than the forced 1.W D3,
gives a move-order independent net on a Black group.  The forced-kill
set is empty.
public_text.3:
{} 

The only points that can put the black corner into atari on move 1 are the
two liberties of C1–C2, B1 and B2.  B1 and B2 are the only moves that touch a
black liberty at all.

1.W B1.  C1–C2 is in atari on B2.  Black is forced to 2.B B2 which
connects A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into the six stone group G.  After 1.W B1 2.B B2
G has the three outside liberties A1 A3 A4 and W B1 is itself in atari on
A1.  3.B A1 captures W B1.  G is then left on A3 A4 B1 and any White
reduction A3 or A4 is met by Black immediately recapturing the net stone
on A4/A3. The A1/B1 race is the familiar snap-back, so no net is forced.

1.W B2.  W B2 is in atari on B1 and C1–C2 is in atari on B1.  The only
useful defence is 2.B B1 which captures the sacrificial W B2 and makes
B1–C1–C2.  After 1.W B2 2.B B1

G1 = B1–C1–C2   L = {A1 , B2}
G2 = A2         L = {A1 , A3 , B2}
G3 = B3–B4      L = {A3 , A4 , B2}

A1 and B2 are suicide for White and the only legal reductions are A3 and
A4.  3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone, 3.W A4 is met by
4.B A3.  In both lines Black can keep the false liberties A1 and B2 and
can always capture the White netting stone first. The A3/A4 exchange is
the snap-back/ko that prevents a forced capture.

A1, A3, A4 are self-atari or are captured at once and touch no black
group in atari. The D1–D2 wall has E1 E2 D3 and is not in atari.  Hence
no first White move creates a capture of a black group against best Black
defence.  The nominal net at B2 is a snap-back and the forced-kill set is
empty.
public_text.6:
{}
The only points that can put a black chain into atari on move 1 are the liberties of the C1-C2 pair, B1 and B2.  

* 1.W B1 → C1-C2 is in atari on B2.  2.B B2 is forced.  The six stones
  A2 B2 B3 B4 C1 C2 become G with L(G) = { A1, A3, A4 } and W B1 is left
  with L = {A1}.  3.B A1 captures W B1.  A3/A4 is a snap-back: 3.W A3 is met
  by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone and 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 5.B A5
  capturing the net stone.  The race for the shared liberty A1 is won by
  Black.

* 1.W B2 → C1-C2 is in atari on B1 and W B2 is in atari on B1.  2.B B1 is
  forced and captures W B2.  After 1.W B2 2.B B1

  G1 = B1-C1-C2  L = {A1, B2}
  G2 = A2        L = {A1, A3, B2}
  G3 = B3-B4     L = {A3, A4, B2}

  A1 and B2 are suicide for White.  3.W A3 is answered by 4.B A4 capturing
  W A3 and 3.W A4 is answered by 4.B A3 followed by 5.B A5 capturing W A4.
  Black can always keep at least two liberties on the left side and can
  always capture the White net stone first.  The same snap-back holds after
  1.W B1.

A1, A3, A4 are captured at once by B B1, B A4, B A3 respectively and never
touch a black group in atari.  The D1-D2 group has the three liberties
E1 E2 D3 and is not atari.  Hence no first White move creates a forced net
on a black group against best defence.
public_text.12:
{}
The only first moves that touch a black liberty are A1 A3 A4 B1 B2.
All of them are met by an immediate black reply that restores at least two
real liberties to the left side and captures the White sacrificial stone.

* 1.W B1 → 2.B B2 connects A2 B3 B4 C1 C2 into G with L={A1,A3,A4},
W B1 is in atari on A1 and 3.B A1 captures it.  G is then left on A3 A4 B1
and 3.W A3/4.W A4 is the classic A3/A4 snap-back.

* 1.W B2 → C1–C2 is in atari on B1 and W B2 is in atari on B1, so
2.B B1 is forced and captures W B2.  After 1.W B2 2.B B1

G1=B1–C1–C2 L={A1,B2}
G2=A2     L={A1,A3,B2}
G3=B3–B4  L={A3,A4,B2}

A1 and B2 are suicide for White.  The only reductions are 3.W A3 and
3.W A4.  3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone and 3.W A4 is
met by 4.B A3, 5.B A5, and the three black complexes always keep the
false liberties A1 and B2.  Black can always keep at least two liberties
on the left side and the D1–D2 White group has E1 E2 D3 .

A1 A3 A4 are immediate captures by Black.  Hence no first White move
forces a capture against best defence and the forced-kill set is empty.
public_text.2:
{} 

The only points that can touch a black liberty on the first move are the
liberties of the C1–C2 pair, B1 and B2.

1.W B2
* 1.W B2  C1–C2 is left with the single liberty B1 and the white stone on
B2 is itself in atari on B1.  2.B B1 is forced, it captures the sacrificial
W B2 and makes B1–C1–C2.  After the capture B2 is empty again.

  B1–C1–C2  L={A1,B2}
  A2       L={A1,A3,B2}
  B3–B4    L={A3,A4,B2}

A1 and B2 are now self-atari for White and B1 is occupied.  The only

3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone; after 4.B A4

A2–B3–B4–A3 L={A1,B2}

are left with the shared liberties A1,B2.  No White move can fill both

met by Black recapturing the net stone.  A1,A3,A4 on the first move are

Hence no first White move forces a capture of a Black group against best

public_text.11:
{} 

With the 4-file corner the white D1–D2 two stone group has the single
breathing point D3.  The C3–C4 wall is connected to it by D3 so that
1.W D3 is the only move which does not lose D1–D2 at once.  
2…B D3 after any 1.W ≠ D3 captures the D1–D2 group at once.

After the forced defence

1.W D3
the white main group becomes D1–D2–D3–C3–C4 with the two liberties
D4, C5.  The three black corner groups are

* C1–C2  L = {B1,B2}
* A2     L = {A1,A3,B2}
* B3–B4  L = {A3,A4,B2}

B1 and B2 are the only points that put a black group into atari on the
first move.

* 1.W B1 → C1–C2 is in atari on B2. 2.B B2 is forced, it connects
A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into a six stone group G with L={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is
now in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1 and the A3/A4 net is a
snap-back: 4.W A3 is met by 5.B A4 which recaptures the net stone and
leaves G alive on A3,A4,B1, etc.

* 1.W B2 → C1–C2 is in atari on B1 and W B2 itself is in atari on B1.
2.B B1 is forced and captures the sacrificial W B2.  After
1.W B2 2.B B1

G1 = B1–C1–C2 L ={A1,B2}
G2 = A2      L ={A1,A3,B2}
G3 = B3–B4   L ={A3,A4,B2}

A1 and B2 are suicide for White and the only legal reductions are
A3 and A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the A3 stone and
3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3, and the three black groups can always keep the
false liberties A1 and B2.  The same snap-back holds after the forced
defence 1.W D3 2.W B1/B2.

A1,A3,A4 are self-atari or are captured at once.  Hence after the
mandatory 1.W D3 White has no move which puts a black group into
unavoidable atari against best Black defence, and any non-defensive
first move loses D1–D2 at once to 2…B D3.  No first white move therefore
initiates a kill that is forced against all Black replies.
public_text.8:
{} 

The right side is the decisive point.  

D1–D2 is a two stone group on the D-file.  With the board closed on the
D side the group has the single liberty D3.  Any first move ≠ D3 is met at
once by 2…B D3 and the D1–D2 group is removed, so a forcing kill must begin
with the defensive

1.W D3

1.W D3 joins D1–D2 to C3–C4.  The combined right wall R = D1 D2 D3 C3 C4 is
now on D4,C5 and R is joined to B5 and D5 through C5.  The three white
groups are therefore mutually weak and the first aggressive reply on the
right is

2…B A5

A5 is legal and puts B5 in atari on C5.  B5 can only be saved by 3.W C5.
3.W C5 merges R, B5 and D5 into one white group G.  After 2…B A5 3.W C5

G = D1 D2 D3 C3 C4 C5 B5 D5

has the single empty neighbour D4.  D4 is a legal capture now:
4…B D4 removes the whole R–B5–D5 complex.  Hence 1.W D3 does not survive
best defence, and in particular it does not give White a forced net on the
left.

With the defence 1.W D3 in place the left side is

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board geometry is now settled: D1–D2 is not in atari. D1 neighbours C1,E1,D2 and D2 neighbours D1,D3,C2,E2, so with C1 and C2 occupied by Black the White group D1–D2–C3–C4–B5–D5 has the free liberties E1,E2,D3,D4,C5 etc. The “must play D3 first or lose D1–D2” line used by Colleagues 10,11,14,2,4,8,9 is therefore based on a false atari premise. The board-size confusion from earlier is resolved and the real first-move candidates that touch a Black liberty are the two liberties of the C1–C2 pair, B1 and B2. A1,A3,A4 touch a Black liberty but are self-atari or are captured at once.

B1 line:
1.W B1 puts C1–C2 in atari on B2 and White B1 itself has the single liberty A1. The only useful Black reply is 2.B B2 which connects A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into six-stone group G with L(G)={A1,A3,A4} and puts W B1 in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures the sacrifice. G is then left on A3,A4,B1 and any White reduction A3/A4 is met by Black recapturing the net stone on A4/A3. This is the classic A3/A4 snap-back and Black can keep ≥2 real liberties.

B2 line:
1.W B2 puts C1–C2 in atari on B1 and W B2 itself is in atari on B1. The only useful defence is 2.B B1 which captures the sacrificial W B2 and makes B1–C1–C2. After 1.W B2 2.B B1
G1=B1–C1–C2 L={A1,B2}
G2=A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
G3=B3–B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
A1 and B2 are suicide for White. The only legal reductions are A3 and A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone; 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3. Black can always keep the false liberties A1 and B2 and recapture the White net stone first. The A3/A4 exchange is again a snap-back/ko.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is A1 top left. Black groups are
* G1=C1-C2 L={B1,B2}
* G2=A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
* G3=B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
White groups are B5 alone, C3-C4 with L={D3,D4,C5}, D1-D2 with L={E1,E2,D3} and D5 alone. D1-D2 is not in atari; the D3 defence myth is false. E1/E2 are real liberties.

The only first moves that touch a black liberty are A1,A3,A4,B1,B2.

* 1.W A3 puts white A3 in atari on A4 and is met by 2.B A4 capturing the net stone. 1.W A1 puts white A1 in atari on B1 and is met by 2.B B1 capturing A1.
* 1.W A4 reduces G3 to {A3,B2}. Black can answer 2.B A3 putting white A4 in atari on A5 and the A3/A4 exchange is the classic snap-back.

B1 and B2 are the only moves that put G1 in atari.

1.W B1 → G1 L={B2}. 2.B B2 is forced; B2 connects A2-B3-B4-C1-C2 into G L={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is now in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1. G is left on A3,A4,B1 and every White reduction A3/A4 is met by Black recapturing the net stone on A4/A3. The A1/B1 race is won by Black.

1.W B2 → G1 L={B1} and W B2 L={B1}. 2.B B1 is forced and captures W B2, making G1'=B1-C1-C2 L={A1,B2}, G2=A2 L={A1,A3,B2}, G3=B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}. A1 and B2 are suicide for White. The only legal reductions are A3 and A4:
3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the A3 stone, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3 putting W A4 in atari on A5. Black can always keep the false liberties A1 and B2 and capture the White net stone first.

Hence B1 and B2 are snap-backs, A1/A3/A4 are self-atari or immediate capture, and no other first move touches a black liberty. With best Black defence the left corner keeps at least two real liberties and every White sacrificial net stone is recapturable first. No first White move forces an unavoidable capture of a Black group; the forced-kill set is empty. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is at least A–E, so the D1–D2 white pair has the real liberties E1,E2,D3, and C3–C4 is connected to it by D3. The right side is therefore not a forced defensive first move and the E-off-board argument used in the earlier reflection is a board-edge misinterpretation. With an open edge the first White move is not forced to be 1.W D3.

The only points that touch a black liberty in the left corner are A1, A3, A4, B1, B2.  The C1–C2 pair lives on B1,B2; A2 lives on A1,A3,B2; B3–B4 lives on A3,A4,B2.  The two ostensibly attacking first moves are B1 and B2.

* 1.W B1. C1–C2 is in atari on B2.  Black is forced to 2.B B2 which connects A2–B2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into G with L(G)={A1,A3,A4} and leaves W B1 in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures W B1.  G is left on A3,A4,B1 and any White net 4.W A3 is met by 5.B A4 recapturing the net stone, 4.W A4 is met by 5.B A3.  The A1/B1 race is the familiar snap-back.

* 1.W B2. C1–C2 is in atari on B1 and W B2 itself is in atari on B1. 2.B B1 is forced and captures W B2, making B1–C1–C2 with L={A1,B2}. After 1.W B2 2.B B1 we have
G1=B1–C1–C2 L={A1,B2}
G2=A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
G3=B3–B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
A1 and B2 are suicide for White. The only legal reductions are A3 and A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the A3 stone, 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3.  Black can always recapture the White net stone first and keep the false liberties A1,B2. The same snap-back holds after any other first move that touches the corner.

A1,A3,A4 are either self-atari or are captured at once and never create a move-order independent atari on a black group. The B1 and B2 sacrifices are snap-backs and the shared liberty A1 can always be kept by Black. No first White move therefore creates a forced net on a black group against best Black defence.

The {B2} / {B1} claims in the current round rely on the E-off-board assumption that D1–D2 is in immediate atari and that D3 is mandatory. With the correct board extension that assumption is false, but even allowing the open edge the B1/B2 lines remain snap-backs. reflection_text.3:
The board geometry is now settled: D1–D2 is not in atari. D1 neighbours C1,E1,D2 and D2 neighbours D1,D3,C2,E2, so with C1 and C2 occupied by Black the White group D1–D2–C3–C4–B5–D5 has the free liberties E1,E2,D3,D4,C5 etc. The “must play D3 first or lose D1–D2” line used by Colleagues 10,11,14,2,4,8,9 is therefore based on a false atari premise. The board-size confusion from earlier is resolved and the real first-move candidates that touch a Black liberty are the two liberties of the C1–C2 pair, B1 and B2. A1,A3,A4 touch a Black liberty but are self-atari or are captured at once.

B1 line:
1.W B1 puts C1–C2 in atari on B2 and White B1 itself has the single liberty A1. The only useful Black reply is 2.B B2 which connects A2–B3–B4–C1–C2 into six-stone group G with L(G)={A1,A3,A4} and puts W B1 in atari on A1. 3.B A1 captures the sacrifice. G is then left on A3,A4,B1 and any White reduction A3/A4 is met by Black recapturing the net stone on A4/A3. This is the classic A3/A4 snap-back and Black can keep ≥2 real liberties.

B2 line:
1.W B2 puts C1–C2 in atari on B1 and W B2 itself is in atari on B1. The only useful defence is 2.B B1 which captures the sacrificial W B2 and makes B1–C1–C2. After 1.W B2 2.B B1
G1=B1–C1–C2 L={A1,B2}
G2=A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
G3=B3–B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
A1 and B2 are suicide for White. The only legal reductions are A3 and A4. 3.W A3 is met by 4.B A4 capturing the net stone; 3.W A4 is met by 4.B A3. Black can always keep the false liberties A1 and B2 and recapture the White net stone first. The A3/A4 exchange is again a snap-back/ko.

Hence both nominally threatening first moves are answered by a forced capture of the White sacrificial stone and a snap-back on A3/A4. No first move puts a Black group into unavoidable atari and no first move creates a move-order independent net. The claims that {B2} initiates a forced kill by Colleagues 1,13,5,7,14 and the claims that {B1} initiates a forced kill by Colleague 11 in round 0 miss the snap-back on A3/A4 and the fact that after 2.B B1 the B1–C1–C2 group still has the real liberty A1.

The majority of the current round, Colleagues 10,11,12,14,2,3,4,6,7,8,9, converge on the empty set {}. The persistent minority {B2} persists from earlier rounds but is refuted by the snap-back analysis. Current belief is that the forced-kill set of first White moves is empty.

reflection_text.11:
{
The left A1 corner is the only fighting area. Black groups start as
C1-C2 L={B1,B2}; A2 L={A1,A3,B2}; B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}.
White right wall D1-D2 L={E1,E2,D3}, C3-C4 L={D3,D4,C5}, B5 L={A5,C5}, D5 L={C5,E5,D4}.
D1-D2 is not in atari and D3 is not a mandatory first defence. The D1-D2 atari / forced D3 defence claim is a myth; E1,E2 give real liberties.

First moves that touch a black liberty are only B1,B2. A1,A3,A4 are self-atari or captured at once and touch no black group in atari. No other point touches a black liberty.

1.W B1
C1-C2 is left on B2 and W B1 is L={A1,B2}. 2.B B2 is legal and connects A2-B2-B3-B4-C1-C2 = G with L(G)={A1,A3,A4} and W B1 is now L={A1}. 3.B A1 captures W B1. G is left on A3,A4,B1 and the A3/A4 snap-back holds: 4.W A3 5.B A4 recaptures the net stone, 4.W A4 5.B A3 recaptures. The A1/B1 race is won by Black.

1.W B2
C1-C2 is left on B1 and W B2 is itself L={B1}. The only saving defence is 2.B B1 which captures the sacrificial W B2 and makes B1-C1-C2.
After 1.W B2 2.B B1
G1 = B1-C1-C2 L={A1,B2}
G2 = A2 L={A1,A3,B2}
G3 = B3-B4 L={A3,A4,B2}
A1 and B2 are suicide for White after the capture. The only legal reductions are A3 and A4 and both are snap-backs: 3.W A3 4.B A4 captures W A3, 3.W A4 4.B A3 captures W A4. Black can always recapture the White net stone first and keep the false liberties A1,B2.

The same snap-back holds for the B1 first move. No first White move puts a Black group into unavoidable atari against best defence. In particular the connection 2.B B2 after 1.W B1 gives Black a six-stone group with three outside liberties and the White stone is recapturable on A1.

Minority B2 claim {B2} persists in Colleague 13. It rests on an error: after 1.W B2 2.B B1 the liberty B2 is empty after the capture and is still a liberty of B1-C1-C2, A2 and B3-B4. The claim that G1 = B1-C1-C2 L={A1} and that B2 is “now white and cannot be used again” is false, and the claimed White control of the A1 race via the right wall is unsupported.

Current consensus after Round 3 is empty forced-kill set {}. B1 and B2 are the strongest reductions but both are classic snap-backs with forced recapture of the White sacrificial stone. No first move initiates a move-order independent kill.
}
